redditSourcedNotes: No reddit or forum content was harvested for this city: the researcher's web budget was exhausted before any query ran, so the draft came from prior knowledge with empty sources. The review stage had a 5-search budget and spent it on the highest-doubt items: (1) 343 Sansome roof garden confirmed as an active POPOS, Mon-Fri 10am-5pm, sign in at the lobby desk; (2) Pier 7 confirmed as an 840 ft public fishing pier but it has no dedicated Wikipedia article, so its title stays null; (3) Salesforce Park hours confirmed from the TJPA (6am-9pm May-Oct, 6am-8pm Nov-Apr), no dedicated Wikipedia article; (4) the Main Library has its own article, 'Main Library (San Francisco)'; (5) City Lights now closes at 10pm, not midnight, so the blurb and tips were corrected. All 14 spots are real, publicly accessible places the reviewer knows; none involve trespassing, derelict sites or active industrial land. Remaining Wikipedia titles (Grand View Park, Bernal Heights Park, Ina Coolbrith Park, Lands End (San Francisco), City Lights Bookstore, Grace Cathedral, San Francisco, National AIDS Memorial Grove, Mount Sutro) are kept on reviewer knowledge of those exact article titles and were not individually search-confirmed. Sources were attached only where a URL actually appeared in a review search result; spots verified from knowledge alone keep an empty sources array rather than invented citations. Hours other than the four confirmed above are best recollection and are marked 'check site'. Safety was tightened: Lands End (unstable bluffs, sneaker waves at Sutro Baths) and the Main Library (surrounding Civic Center/Tenderloin blocks after dark) were moved to caution alongside Bernal Heights Park.

spots.name: Grand View Park
spots.blurb: A tiny sand-dune summit ringed by a wooden staircase, sitting above the Inner Sunset with the city fanned out below: Golden Gate Park, the bridge, Ocean Beach and downtown in one slow turn. Locals climb the 16th Avenue Tiled Steps and keep going to sit on the bench or the low stone wall at the top. It draws a handful of people at sunset and is nearly empty at sunrise.
spots.tips: Enter from the top of the Tiled Steps at 16th Ave and Moraga St, then take the wooden stairs off 14th Ave. Bring a windbreaker; the summit is exposed and often socked in with fog on summer afternoons.

safety.note: Residential hilltop reached by steep stairs; the summit path is unlit, so go before dark.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia title matches the SF park article to the reviewer's knowledge but was not search-confirmed.

spots.name: Bernal Heights Park
spots.blurb: A grassy, treeless hill with a dirt loop road around it and a 360-degree view of downtown, the bay, Twin Peaks and, on clear days, both bridges. It is a dog-walkers' and neighbors' hill rather than a tourist stop, so the mood is people sitting in the grass with coffee. Sunset from the west-facing slope is the local ritual, and the city lights after dark are the reward for the climb.
spots.tips: Walk up from Folsom St via Bernal Heights Blvd or from Cortland Ave; the rock outcrop on the north side is the best perch. Grass is dry and prickly by late summer, so bring something to sit on.

safety.note: Paths are unlit and the loop road has no railings on the downhill side. Plenty of neighbors around at dusk; after dark bring a headlamp, stay on the loop road and go with a friend.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia title not search-confirmed.

spots.name: Ina Coolbrith Park
spots.blurb: A steep pocket park of terraces, stairways and overgrown greenery on the east flank of Russian Hill, named for California's first poet laureate. Benches on each level look out at the Bay Bridge, Coit Tower and the water, and most of the people who find it are climbing the Vallejo Street steps. Early mornings you can often have it to yourself with the sun coming up over the East Bay.
spots.tips: Enter at Vallejo and Taylor Streets; the top terrace has the best bench. It is all stairs, so skip it if knees are an issue, and do not linger after dark since there is no lighting.

safety.note: Quiet residential stairs; unlit, so visit in daylight or at dusk.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia title not search-confirmed.

spots.name: Lands End
spots.blurb: The rugged northwest corner of the city, where the Coastal Trail runs along cypress-covered bluffs above the Golden Gate strait with the bridge sliding in and out of view. The Sutro Baths ruins at the bottom are the classic place to sit on the old concrete walls and watch the Pacific at sunset. It is well known, but big enough that a few minutes past the Lookout the crowd thins to joggers and neighbors walking dogs.
spots.tips: Start at the Lands End Lookout on Point Lobos Ave; take the stairs down to the Baths for sunset, or walk east to Eagle's Point for the bridge view. Bring layers, the wind is relentless.
spots.hours: trails dawn-dusk; Lookout visitor center roughly 9am-5pm

safety.note: The bluffs are unstable and the trail is unlit: stay on the fenced Coastal Trail, finish before dark, and keep off the rocks below Sutro Baths, where sneaker waves have swept people into the water.

spots.verifyNote: National Park Service site kept on reviewer knowledge. Raised to caution for the documented cliff and sneaker-wave hazards. Wikipedia title not search-confirmed.

spots.name: Pier 7
spots.blurb: An 840-foot public fishing pier, lamp-lined and edged with iron railings and wooden benches, that pokes straight out into the bay near the Ferry Building, with the Bay Bridge lights on one side and the Transamerica Pyramid framed at the landward end. Locals fish off the end, joggers use it as a turnaround, and everyone else sits with a coffee watching ferries come and go. It is one of the few places to be right on the water at night with real lighting around you.
spots.tips: The benches at the far end catch the sunrise behind the Bay Bridge; at night the whole Embarcadero promenade is lit and busy. It is exposed, so bring a jacket even in summer.

sources.label: Pier Fishing in California: Pier 7 - San Francisco

safety.note: Lamp-lit the whole way out and railed on both edges, with the Embarcadero promenade lit behind it. It is an 840-foot dead end over deep, cold water, so at night the far end is a long walk back with only one way off.

spots.verifyNote: Search confirmed the pier (dedicated 1990, public fishing pier). No dedicated Wikipedia article exists, only 'List of piers in San Francisco', so title stays null.

spots.name: Salesforce Park
spots.blurb: A 5.4-acre park on the roof of the Salesforce Transit Center, four stories above the streets, with a half-mile walking loop, lawns, an amphitheater and gardens that run through redwoods, desert plants and a wetland. Office workers eat lunch here and then it empties out, so an afternoon on the grass with the towers leaning in overhead feels surprisingly private. No admission, just an elevator or the free gondola from Mission Street.
spots.tips: Ride the gondola at Mission and Fremont or take the corner elevators; the quietest lawn is at the east end. It closes at 8pm in winter and 9pm in summer, so plan evening visits accordingly.

sources.label: Transbay Joint Powers Authority: Salesforce Park
San Francisco Travel: Guide to Salesforce Park

safety.note: Staffed park with security on site; closes in the evening.

spots.verifyNote: Hours confirmed from the TJPA. No dedicated Wikipedia article for the park (it is covered within the Salesforce Transit Center article), so title stays null.

spots.name: San Francisco Main Library
spots.blurb: A big, bright civic library organized around a five-story atrium, with reading rooms on every floor, tables in the stacks and an upper art-and-music floor that stays quiet most of the day. It is free, warm, has wifi and outlets, and nobody minds if you sit with a book for hours. On a rainy day this is where a lot of the city goes to think.
spots.tips: Upper-floor window seats along Fulton St get the best light; the ground floor is busiest. Enter from Larkin St or Grove St; the surrounding plaza is not the place to linger.
spots.hours: Tue-Thu 9am-8pm; Mon and Sat 10am-6pm; Fri and Sun 12-6pm (check site)

sources.label: SF Civic Center CBD: Main Branch of the San Francisco Public Library
Time Out: San Francisco Main Library

safety.note: Inside is calm, with security at every entrance. The library closes at 6pm most days and 8pm at the latest, and the plaza out front is wide open and empties once the civic buildings shut, so use the Larkin or Grove St entrances and the Civic Center BART/Muni station directly beneath it rather than walking to a stop further off.

spots.verifyNote: Search confirmed the dedicated Wikipedia article 'Main Library (San Francisco)'. Raised to caution for the surrounding blocks; hours are best recollection.

spots.name: City Lights Bookstore
spots.blurb: The Beat-era bookstore on Columbus Avenue is three creaky floors of books with chairs tucked between the shelves and hand-lettered signs telling you to sit down and read. The upstairs Poetry Room, with its wooden chairs and window over Jack Kerouac Alley, is the spot: nobody hurries you. It stays open until 10pm every night, which makes it a rare quiet indoor place to sit late in the evening.
spots.tips: Go after 8pm on a weeknight to have the Poetry Room nearly to yourself; the basement is the quietest during the day. Vesuvio across the alley is the obvious follow-up if you want a drink.

safety.note: Broadway and Columbus are lively late; the store itself is calm and well-staffed.

spots.verifyNote: Search confirmed hours are now 10am-10pm daily (draft said midnight; blurb and tips corrected) and the Wikipedia title.

spots.name: Grace Cathedral
spots.blurb: A huge, cool, quiet Gothic-style cathedral at the top of Nob Hill that is open to visitors most days, with pews under stained glass, a Keith Haring altarpiece and two labyrinths, one indoors and one outside on the plaza. People come in to sit in the silence, walk the labyrinth slowly or just get out of the wind. Suggested donation only.
spots.tips: The outdoor labyrinth on the front plaza is open even when the doors are shut; the indoor one is at the back of the nave. Weekday afternoons are emptiest; Sunday mornings are services, and the nave closes to visitors during events.
spots.hours: visitor hours roughly 10am-5pm daily, Sunday from about 8am; closed to visitors during services and events (check site)

safety.note: Staffed and calm; Huntington Park across the street is a lit, well-used spot to sit afterward.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia title is the exact article name to the reviewer's knowledge; hours are best recollection.

spots.name: Farley's
spots.blurb: A neighborhood coffeehouse on 18th Street that has anchored Potrero Hill since 1989, with a long counter, mismatched tables, a magazine rack and a bench out front where dog owners linger. People work quietly for hours, read the paper and chat with the baristas by name. The block is sleepy and the view down the hill toward the bay is a bonus.
spots.tips: Weekday afternoons are calmest; weekend mornings fill up with strollers and dogs. Grab a window seat, then walk two blocks up 18th St for the skyline view.
spots.verifyNote: Long-running cafe at 1315 18th St kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent); hours unverified.

spots.name: National AIDS Memorial Grove
spots.blurb: A wooded dell in the eastern half of Golden Gate Park set aside as a living memorial, with redwoods, ferns, a dry creek bed and a stone Circle of Friends carved with names. It is designed for contemplation, so it stays hushed even when the park around it is busy, and there are benches and boulders to sit on for as long as you like. People come here to read, to remember someone, or just to hear nothing but birds.
spots.tips: Enter from Bowling Green Drive off Nancy Pelosi Drive near the tennis courts; mid-morning on a weekday is near-total quiet. Keep voices low, it is a memorial.

safety.note: Secluded and unlit; leave before dusk.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia title not search-confirmed.

spots.name: Mount Sutro Open Space Reserve
spots.blurb: A dense eucalyptus forest on a hill in the middle of the city, owned by UCSF and threaded with soft dirt trails that feel like a mountain park, with fog dripping off the trees on summer afternoons. The Historic Trail and the summit clearing get a few hikers and dog walkers and not many others. There are log benches and a small rock garden at the top; it is one of the easiest places in San Francisco to forget you are in a city.
spots.tips: Enter at Stanyan and 17th St or from Medical Center Way behind UCSF; the summit is about a 20-minute climb. Trails get muddy after rain and there is no lighting, so go in daylight.

safety.note: Unlit forest trails; daylight only, and tell someone your route if going solo.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). Wikipedia article 'Mount Sutro' covers the hill and its open space reserve; not search-confirmed.

spots.name: 343 Sansome Rooftop Garden
spots.blurb: A privately owned public open space (POPOS) on the 15th floor of an office building, reached by an elevator from the lobby: a landscaped terrace with tables, benches, planters and a tiled obelisk by Joan Brown looking out at the Transamerica Pyramid and across the FiDi rooftops. It is open to anyone on weekdays and few people outside the building know about it, so lunchtime brings a crowd of office workers and the rest of the day is nearly empty. Bring a book and a coffee from the street.
spots.tips: Enter the lobby at 343 Sansome, sign in with security at the front desk and take the elevator to 15; weekdays only, 10am-5pm. Combine with other FiDi POPOS rooftops like One Montgomery.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 10am-5pm; sign in at the lobby desk

sources.label: Downtown SF Partnership: 343 Sansome St public open space
Golden Gate Xpress: Where's the POPO?

safety.note: Office building with lobby security; closed weekends and holidays.

spots.verifyNote: Search confirmed the POPOS is active, Mon-Fri 10am-5pm with front-desk sign-in. Lowkey score trimmed from 5 to 4 because it fills at lunchtime.

spots.name: Japantown Peace Plaza
spots.blurb: An open plaza under the five-tiered Peace Pagoda between the Japan Center malls, with wide steps, low walls and benches where people eat takeout, read and watch the neighborhood go by. It is lit at night and surrounded by shops and restaurants that stay open into the evening, with Kinokuniya bookstore a few steps away. Calm rather than lively, it is a good place to sit after dark without going anywhere in particular.
spots.tips: Sit on the steps facing the pagoda at dusk and grab a bun from the bakeries inside the mall. Avoid festival weekends like Cherry Blossom in April if you want it quiet.

safety.note: Well-lit, with mall entrances and restaurants around it into the evening.

spots.verifyNote: Kept on reviewer knowledge (no search spent). No dedicated Wikipedia article for the plaza itself; the district article does not qualify, so title stays null.
